metadata.case_name: LI YUET YEE AND OTHERS v. NG CHI HANG

source:
2. ……His wife, and younger son sustained severe injury whereas he himself had no physical injury at all. However, he developed insomnia, crying spells, irritability, nightmares, loss of interest, suicidal idea, decreased appetite and weight loss after the accident. He had recollection of the scene in dreams.

3. A diagnosis of Depressive episode was made. He was prescribed medications.

4. He was subsequently followed-up on 3.11.03, 29.12.03, 1.3.04 and 13.5.04. His mental condition was noted to have significant improvement. Permanent disability is not expected.

30. ……

30.1. He has suffered from posttraumatic stress disorder ……

30.2. He has difficulty adjusting to the aftermaths of the accident including his wife’s and son’s disability. He is depressed and worried by their problems. The depressive symptoms that he is having consist of depressed mood, irritability, feelings of difficulty coping, pessimistic ideas, lack of confidence and motivation, lack of interest in sex and activities, and sleep problems ……

31. His mental condition was at its worst for a few months after the accident. He was on the verge of nervous break-down. His mental condition has shown improvement with time and after psychiatric treatment. He is displaying residual symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder currently ……

32. He is mentally capable of returning to work at the pre-accident job. His working efficiency is affected by the lack of confidence, difficulty concentrating, bad memory and tremors of hands. His work is also affected by his decreased motivation, decreased drive for social interaction and his irritability. The appropriate period of sick leave from a psychiatric point of view is one year from the date of the accident.

33. ……He will continue to suffer from residual mental problems for a few years as the accident left a mark on his mind and some of his wife’s and son’s disability are permanent.

37. We believe that the degree of permanent impairment to the whole person of Mr. LAM is about 7%. The loss of earning capacity is estimated to be about 7% after completion of the recommended psychotherapies.

manifestations.description: recollection of the scene in dreams
lack of interest in sex and activities
on the verge of nervous break-down
marital relationship affected; difficulty communicating with his wife

losses.description: The whole family relationship has been affected by the accident; the Husband has become irritable and withdrawn. Awarded: $50,000.
Unable to do sophisticated jewellery any more; loss of congenial employment. Awarded: $120,000.
Reduced working efficiency due to lack of confidence, difficulty concentrating and bad memory affecting work and earning capacity.

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life

losses.description: Pre-trial loss of earnings (calculation): $20,000 x 12 = $240,000; ($20,000 - $9,000) x 46 = $506,000; Total pre-trial loss of earnings awarded: $746,000.
Post-trial (future) loss of earnings awarded: $1,320,000 [($20,000 - $9,000) x 12 x 10].

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Medical and travelling expenses agreed and ordered: $270 medical and $1,400 travelling; total $1,670.

losses.category: Loss of ability to enjoy food and drink
Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Future medical expenses awarded: $102,500; future travelling expenses awarded: $3,150; total future medical and travelling expenses: $105,650.

comparable_cases.case_name: Tsui Ho (2nd Plaintiff) v The Incorporated Owners of Albert House & Ors
comparable_cases.injury_description: Victim died in the accident; impairment of the whole person was 30% before treatment, and 20% after treatment.
